title: Epistemological Sprawl
definition: The disproportionate expansion of philosophical and epistemological concepts in a knowledge graph compared to scientific and empirical concepts.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine a garden where the seeds of ideas grow uncontrollably. If it only plants seeds of philosophical questions without any scientific answers, the garden becomes a mess with no clear path or fruit.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: Epistemological Sprawl occurs when the knowledge graph expands primarily with abstract concepts, particularly philosophical and epistemological ones, without a corresponding expansion of scientific and empirical concepts.
difficulty_levels.expert: Epistemological Sprawl challenges the integrity of the knowledge graph by creating a feedback loop. The more philosophical concepts exist, the more philosophical connections Mistral finds, further tilting the graph toward abstraction. This leads to a lack of grounded concepts and weakens cross-domain reasoning.

extra_fields.insight: The disproportionate expansion of philosophical concepts may hinder the graph's ability to provide deep, practical insights.
